column1: # what each frame-lane control is for: its one intended fault kind, and that
# kind's first failure, taken from the frozen pin named in the line column.
# collateral names the other kinds that pin raises: the same defect arriving
# A CONTROL CASE ASSERTS THREE ROWS FROM EACH ROW HERE: the intended kind gt0,
# that kind's first-failure text eq, and faults.raised set -- the intended kind
# TOGETHER WITH its collateral kinds, by name and with no counts. The collateral
# kinds are asserted as members of that set, never by count.
# The set is not droppable: clear-skip and clear-drop-counters share their
# intended kind and their first-failure text byte for byte, so on the first two
# rows alone each would pass the other's expectation. They differ only in what
# else they raise. clear-drop-counters is the 7a1df0b vacuity guard, so without
# the set it is exactly the case a wrong implementation passes.
# A ROW WHOSE line IS - HAS NO PIN: the control is newer than the frozen
# revision, so its intended kind and its raised set are DECLARED in controls.rb
# from what the control changes, and its first failure is TBD until a run gives
# frame-lane pins of tests/doom-core/tick.sh, extracted by tests/doom-core/harness/pins.rb

column6: why
the schedule is walked backwards, so every push, mark and check still agrees and only the screen the executor draws can differ
the fuzz phase is one later, which changes drawn pixels and nothing else; the first failure is the first frame with a fuzz column
the executor is given the previous frame's span bank, so the banks the pushes filled still agree and only the screen differs
the schedule entry is written where nothing reads it, which the push comparison sees at the second push; the planes and the screen follow from it

column3: cspan status 3 BOUNDS masked tic 0 frame 0
column6: wall pushes are issued as span pushes, whose records name rows past the screen. What the control is for is that a COMPILED entry refuses them -- the span check answers BOUNDS -- which is why it cannot run on the Ruby route at all
phase 1 is marked from the span counter instead of the wall counter, so the mark differs; the check tables built to that mark differ in turn

column3: pwall status 4 CAPACITY wall tic 0 frame 0
column6: the wall bank is given a capacity of 100, and what the control is for is the refusal at the 101st push. With a compiled entry that is a CAPACITY status, not the port's own push-capacity, which stays 0 there

column3: frame 0 after check_disjoint xcount[261] port 1 original 2
column6: the phase-0 wall table is built from the second job, so the interval table differs and nothing upstream of it does
the span table is left unbuilt on odd frames, so its statistics differ; the first failure is the first odd frame
every plane 1 more than a multiple of 3 is left undrawn, which the per-plane comparison sees; the missing spans then move the pushes, checks and screen
the next plane's arrays are drawn in this plane's place, which the per-plane comparison sees as a different picnum, height and light
every plane's height is loaded 1.0 high, which the per-plane comparison sees; the spans it emits then differ and the screen with them

column3: frame 1 after clear_planes lastvisplane port 10 original 0
column6: clear_planes is left out on odd frames, so the cells it should have written keep the values the frame before left

column3: frame 1 after clear_planes lastvisplane port 10 original 0
column6: the four counter writes are undone after the port's clear. It is the 7a1df0b vacuity guard: before that commit the port started from the written value, so deleting the writes changed nothing observable

column3: frame 0 after clear_planes floorclip[0] port 0 original 168
column6: the clip writes are undone after the port's clear, which the per-field clear comparison sees at floorclip[0] in frame 0

the walk is handed a private skyflatnum buffer holding -1, which no plane's picnum equals, so the walk recognizes no plane as sky and draws every sky plane as an ordinary flat. What the control is for is that the walk's own sky-plane count then disagrees with the original's, which the comparison after the walk sees; the spans it emits where the original pushed columns move the pushes, the check tables and the screen

the walk is handed a private skytexturemid buffer 1.0 high, so every sky column is pushed with a wrong texturemid and nothing else moves: the same planes are drawn and the same number of columns pushed. The wall-bank comparison of the sky columns is what sees it, and only the screen the executor draws from those jobs follows

the walk is handed a private pspriteiscale buffer 1 higher, so every sky column is pushed with a wrong iscale, one field over from sky-texmid's and with the same shape: the wall-bank comparison of the sky columns sees it, and only the screen follows

the walk's lastvisplane cell is loaded one lower than the original's, so the walk stops one plane short of the visplanes the original drew. What the control is for is that the missing plane leaves the counters the walk reports short of the original's, which the comparison after the walk sees; the spans and schedule entries it never pushed move the pushes, the check tables and the screen
